info.bio: Cornershop son una banda británica de indie formada en Leicester en 1992 por el nacido en Wolverhampton Tjinder Singh (cantante, compositor y dholaki), su hermano Avtar Singh (bajo, voz), David Chambers (batería) y Ben Ayres (guitarra, teclados y tamboura). Los tres primeros habían sido miembros de la banda de Preston General Havoc, que había publicado un single ("Fast Jaspal EP") en 1991. El nombre de la banda se originó de un estereotipo sobre los asiáticos británicos, que dice que siempre tienen tiendas en todas las esquinas (corner = esquina, shop = tienda). Su música es una fusión de música india, indie rock británico y dance electrónico. . User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

podcast.title: Band's Longevity Outside North America
podcast.body: While "Brimful of Asha" was their only major alt-rock hit, Cornershop has remained active and "a thing" outside of North America, with the band still together. "And while they have remained a thing outside of North America, band is still together, there only major alt-rock radio hits anywhere has been brimful of Asha from 1997."

srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Recording Anecdote
podcast.body: The recording sessions for "Brimful of Asha" were notable for the use of "several pounds of pot." The engineer assigned to the sessions reportedly smoked so much "dope" that he became "freaked out" and required medical assistance. "The engineer assigned to the sessions spoke so much dope and got so freaked out that he actually needed medical assistance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Reference to Asha Bhosle
podcast.body: The "Asha" in the song's title, "Brimful of Asha," refers to Asha Bhosle, renowned as Bollywood's most famous playback singer. Playback singers perform the vocals for songs in Bollywood films, with actors typically lip-syncing the performances on screen. Asha Bhosle is credited with performing over 12,000 songs for Indian films. "And the Asha in the song is a reference to Asha Bosley, who was Bollywood's most famous playback singer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: The Pitch Shift Experiment
podcast.body: A record label executive identified that the initial mix of "Brimful of Asha" was "a touch too slow." Instead of re-recording, which would have been time-consuming and required more resources, the label opted for a simpler fix: pitching up the master tape slightly. This adjustment, performed by Fat Boy Slim, was critical in making the song a hit. "After listening to it a bunch of times, someone at their record label said, you know, I know what's wrong. It's just a touch to slow."
